entities.summary: Zhang Juzheng was a prominent grand secretary during the reigns of Ming emperors Longqing and Wanli, serving from 1567 to 1582. He passed the highest level of official examinations in 1547 and was granted the rank of jinshi, marking a significant milestone in his career. As grand secretary, he played a crucial role in shaping the imperial administration and was responsible for several key policies. His tenure saw the implementation of various reforms, including the reorganization of the imperial examination system and the establishment of a new system of taxation. Zhang Juzheng's legacy continued to shape the Ming dynasty's governance even after his death in 1582, with his reforms serving as a model for future generations of officials. The Longqing Emperor, in particular, came to rely heavily on Zhang Juzheng's counsel, and his influence helped to solidify the emperor's position. Zhang Juzheng's own reputation as a skilled administrator and statesman endured, with many of his contemporaries praising his wisdom and integrity. The Ming dynasty's fortunes began to decline soon after his death, but Zhang Juzheng's contributions to the empire's governance remained an important factor in the dynasty's eventual collapse.
